messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Eval gate 'prod-quality' TRIPPED for model redwood-7b-quant (gate=prod-quality). Signals: output-drift + safety-regression. gate_score=0.38 (threshold=0.6). PagerDuty PD-INC9876 fired to oncall. Automated mitigations attempted: none (canary routing active). <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/eval-gate|runbook>
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty PD-INC9876 acknowledged by alice.m :white_check_mark:
alice.m: Ack'd — I'm on it. Grabbed the traces, starting impact triage. Anyone seeing customer errors? @diana plz coordinate comms if we confirm user-visible issues.
ben_r: I'm watching traffic. Canary share jumped from 0.1 -> 0.25 in last 5m due to recent rollout. Latency unimpacted, but embedding quality drift flagged by evals. Recommending immediate traffic routing to stable variant and disable canary.
carlos: I'll take lead on rollback/reroute. Plan: 1) flip canary off 2) route 100% -> redwood-3b-stable 3) clear per-customer cached KVs to avoid stale prompts. Running commands now.
alice.m: Logs/command I'm running:
```
# route traffic to stable
redwoodctl traffic set --model redwood-7b-quant --percent 0 --target redwood-3b-stable
# confirm rollout
redwoodctl traffic status --model redwood-7b-quant
```

sre-bot: autoscaler note: 3 canary pods failed healthchecks in last 3m, reason: kvcache OOM in tensorize step. Suggest limiting concurrency on canary until we stabilize.
alice.m: PD ack, running route command now. Output:
```
> routing updated: redwood-7b-quant canary=0% -> success
> new default target = redwood-3b-stable
```
diana: Noted customers with elevated error/quality alerts: Acme Payments (prod), NovaRetail (canary traffic), internal integration tests failing for marketplace search. I'm drafting a short note to impacted accounts; will hold until we have mitigation confirmed.
ben_r: After routing, eval-gate score improved to 0.72 on latest sample; safety flags reduced. Looks like the new canary quantized kernels caused the regression.
alice.m: Running quick smoke eval across sample prompts to confirm. Command/summary:
```
# sample eval
python tools/eval_gate_check.py --model redwood-3b-stable --suite prod-sanity --samples 200
# result: pass (0.78)
```
product-ops: Severity? Customer-visible? We need to decide SEV2 vs SEV3 for comms & SRE priority.
carlos: Given Acme Payments saw degraded suggestions (non-blocking) but no outages, I'm classifying SEV2 since it impacts revenue-critical experience. Will spin up detailed incident ticket.
diana: Creating incident ticket and customer email. Draft snippet:
"We detected a quality regression during a model canary rollout affecting suggestion quality for a small subset of requests. Traffic has been routed to a stable model variant and we're continuing validation. No data exposure. We will follow up with timeline and root cause."
alice.m: Noting root cause candidate: quantized kernel change + KV cache edge-case for long context. I'll open PR revert and hold on further canaries. Quick mitigation steps recorded in runbook entry.
sre-bot: mitigation actions executed: traffic reroute, canary disabled, canary pods drained. Autoscaler back to normal.
pagerduty-bot: PD-INC9876 resolved by alice.m — status: mitigated. :white_check_mark:
alice.m: Marking incident as mitigated. Follow-ups: 1) postmortem (owner=carlos) 2) rollback PR + stricter pre-rollout evals (owner=alice.m) 3) update eval-gate to include KV long-context tests (owner=product-ops).
diana: I'll notify Acme + NovaRetail with the drafted note and offer a follow-up sync. Putting SEV2 incident in calendar for postmortem review tomorrow.
product-ops: Thanks all. Any temporary customer workarounds we should recommend? If they see noisy suggestions, ask them to set model pin to `redwood-3b-stable` until we confirm fix.
alice.m: Filed links:
- incident ticket: https://redwood.internal/incidents/PD-INC9876
- runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/eval-gate
- revert PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4592
carlos: I'll start the postmortem draft and include CLS traces and eval diffs. Closing thread here once docs posted. Great coordination — thanks team. :pray:
